description: Historical backfill, not the forward record: the features of past sessions were reconstructed from today's download for the stocks listed today and matched with the returns that followed. Survivorship-biased preliminary reference; read the limitations.
provider: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial; split- and dividend-adjusted, auto_adjust=True); yfinance 1.8.0

universe.note: Stocks listed on the run date only; delisted, acquired and renamed companies are absent.

top_dollar_volume.description: The 500 ranked stocks with the highest avg_dollar_volume_50d on D (all of them when fewer are ranked). RS groups use the percentile within the whole ranked pool.

eligible_pool.description: Every ranked stock of D (price, dollar-volume and history floors): the comparison tier.

limitations: Survivorship: the universe is the stocks listed today. Companies that were large and liquid in the past and were later acquired, taken private or failed are absent, so the results are too favourable. The bias is larger for absolute statements (pool_excess_pct, the excess of stocks passing the template) than for spreads between groups, but spreads are not free of it: among weak stocks only those that survived are counted.

A reconstruction, not the forward record: no snapshot of these days was ever published. It is a preliminary reference kept apart from validation/summary.json and must not be merged with it or quoted as the project's forward result.

Prices are split- and dividend-adjusted as of the download date. Returns, moving-average comparisons and distances from the high are unaffected by a later adjustment, but the price floor and the dollar-volume floor and ranking are applied to adjusted levels, which differ from the prices of that day.
Returns run from the close of D, the same close the features use, so the entry was not obtainable. No commission, spread, market impact or tax is deducted.
Cross-sectional average excess returns of groups, not a strategy backtest: no entry or exit rule, position sizing, turnover or capacity is modelled.

Multiple comparisons: two tiers, several horizons, slices and metrics are tested on one stretch of history, each with its own 95% interval. Some intervals exclude zero by chance alone and nothing is adjusted for it.
Averages are equal-weighted and sensitive to bad prints and extreme moves; rank_ic is reported beside them as the more robust reference.

Only rows at least h sessions apart carry the interval, starting from the first evaluation day (one of several possible starting phases). The interval treats them as independent. A slice covers few distinct episodes (the sessions below the benchmark average are mostly one bear market), so its periods are less independent than that, and a year slice rarely reaches min_non_overlapping_periods.
A stock without a bar on D+h is counted in missing_pct and left out of every average, never filled.
Unofficial data (Yahoo Finance through yfinance). A descriptive study of features and rankings: not a trading strategy, not a forecast and not investment advice.
